summary: The prepared main-base checkout already contains the cross-chunk prefix holdback fix from upstream PR #34458. Added Qwen3-specific regression coverage comparing accumulated streaming channels with whole-message parsing across every two-chunk split and all 128 partitions of the internal </think> boundaries. A temporary restoration of the pre-fix flush behavior reproduced tag leakage, final-answer misclassification, and the detector remaining in reasoning until a later tool token; restoring the current implementation makes the regression pass.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before simulation using the historical behavior that flushed all mixed reasoning/tag-prefix text. Fourteen subcases failed: </think> and final content leaked into reasoning, including chunks ending in reasoning</th. Raw output: reports/j-10a8b99853ad/raw/pre_fix_qwen3_regression.txt

Current checked-out parser with the new Qwen3 regression: 11 tests and 246 subtests passed, including every two-chunk boundary and all 128 internal </think> partition masks compared with one-shot parsing. Raw output: reports/j-10a8b99853ad/raw/final_chunk_invariance.txt

gpu_execution.evidence: The defect and regression are deterministic CPU-only string parsing in python/sglang/srt/parser/reasoning_parser.py; no model inference, kernel, numerical GPU output, or GPU claim was needed or performed.

remaining_limitations: No live Qwen3 model server was launched; verification covers the actual checked-out parser implementation directly rather than end-to-end generation.
The infinite-generation symptom is not time-reproduced with a model; the exact causal parser failure is reproduced as loss of the end marker and misclassification of final content.
The runtime fix predates this branch; this change adds missing Qwen3-specific regression coverage rather than a new production-code fix.
